evidence: Clear separation into core, estoque, and produto modules, each implementing layered structure (models, views, forms, admin, urls, templates)
Directory depth of 4 reflects typical layered layout: project/layer/app/sublayer (e.g., projeto/produto/actions)
Low average fan-out (1.64) indicates loose coupling and layer-based isolation
Views import from models, forms, and other modules in same layer or lower layers, not cross-layer peer dependencies
Django's built-in MVT (Model-View-Template) aligns with layered architecture where presentation, business logic, and data layers are separated
No external ports/adapters or application-core boundary patterns typical of hexagonal architecture
risks: Tight coupling to Django framework may reduce testability and flexibility for domain logic
Templating logic mixed with view logic in Django views may violate strict separation of concerns
No explicit ports/adapters boundaries may hinder integration with non-web interfaces in future
